title: Incident Orchestration Decision Canvas and Runbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This page documents a combined decision canvas and runnable playbook for on-call responders at Redwood Inference. The intent is to give a clear, SLO-driven decision process that: 1) shortens time-to-containment, 2) reduces noisy escalations, and 3) improves evidence collection for post-incident analysis. Use this page as the primary guide when an active incident affects customer-facing inference services (hosted API, Dedicated, or Private control plane).

Scope

- Applies to incidents that impact latency, availability, correctness (quality regressions), or billing/quotas for inference endpoints.
- Does NOT replace service-specific runbooks for deployment, onboarding, or infra reconfiguration; it is the orchestration layer to choose which runbook and communications path to use.

Quick facts and SLO thresholds (production)

- Availability SLO: 99.95% (per-region, 30d rolling).
- Latency SLO: p99 < 350ms for short-form generate endpoints; p99 < 700ms for long-sequence pipelines.
- Error budget alert: Trigger when 7-day rolling availability drops below 99.9% or error-rate increase > 2x baseline for 30 minutes.
- Severity mapping:
  - Sev-0: Global outage impacting >50% of traffic or all control plane requests – page exec & Exec Bridge.
  - Sev-1: Major degradation (SLO breach risk within 1 hour) impacting production customers – Incident Bridge.
  - Sev-2: Partial degradation or isolated customer impact – Slack triage and owner-led response.
  - Sev-3: Minor non-customer impacting issues, backlog tickets.

Roles & ownership

- First Responder (Pager): Acknowledge within 5 minutes. Primary responsibilities: initial triage, evidence collection, stabilize or escalate.
- Incident Lead (IL): Assumes orchestration for incident run until handoff. Owns timeline, communications cadence, and action tracking.
- Engineering SRE: Implements mitigations, applies capacity or routing changes, validates fallbacks.
- Product/CS Liaison: Drafts customer-facing messages and pulls impacted customer list.
- On-call Manager: Ensures correct escalation, rotates relievers if incident extends beyond shift.

Decision Canvas: How to pick the remediation path

Use the following questions in order. Answer quickly and use the branching guidance to select the right runbook and comms path.

1) Detect: Is this an alert (automated) or a customer report?
  - If alert and metric crosses severity thresholds (see Quick facts), continue.
  - If customer report and localized: start Sev-2 triage; verify scope via request logs.

2) Scope: Is impact region-wide or customer-scoped?
  - Region-wide -> consider routing, capacity, or control-plane failure runbooks.
  - Customer-scoped -> follow escalation matrix to platform & account teams; consider temporary exception or throttling.

3) Velocity: Is the degradation rapidly worsening (exponential error growth or rising latency trend)?
  - If yes -> escalate to Incident Lead and open a dedicated bridge.

4) Containment feasibility: Can we reduce blast radius with routing flags, model-fallback, or circuit-breakers?
  - If yes -> implement containment (see Containment steps). If not, escalate to infrastructure leads.

5) Recovery path: Is a fast rollback or failover available (canary rollback, previous model version, or alternate region)?
  - If yes -> run Recovery Execution template.
  - If no -> run Mitigation & Stabilization template and plan RTO > 1 hour.

Runbook templates (copyable blocks)

A) Containment (apply immediately if feasible)
1. Toggle prefix/KV cache passthrough for the affected model pool (console CLI: redwood cache set --pool <pool> --mode passthrough).
2. Apply route-level throttles to limit new sessions to 30% of normal traffic for the affected pool.
3. Activate model-fallback: route low-priority traffic to quantized/compatible variant.
4. If OOM or GPU errors present, drain impacted nodes from serving group and shift traffic to standby capacity.

B) Recovery Execution (rollback/failover)
1. Verify available previous model or deployment snapshot timestamped in the catalog.
2. Initiate canary rollback using the Console: rollouts create --service <svc> --target <version> --canary 10%.
3. Monitor p95/p99 latency and error-rate for 5 minutes. If stable, ramp to 50% for 3m, then full.
4. If rollback fails, revert and fallback to circuit-breaker + staging capacity.

C) Mitigation & Stabilization (when rollback not possible)
1. Temporarily increase autoscale target for Dedicated pools by +25% (owner: infra).
2. Reduce model max_tokens/sequence on heavy pipelines to reduce per-request work.
3. Enable degraded-mode responses: include structured field "warning": "degraded_serving" for downstream clients.
4. Open ticket for engineering change and assign immediate action items with owners and ETA.

Containment checklist (evidence to collect before modifying production)

- Incident timestamp, originating alert ID, scope (regions/tenants), and request sample.
- Relevant metric graphs (latency p50/p95/p99, errors, qps) and trace ids for 3 sample requests across affected timeframe.
- Cluster/node logs (stderr/stdout), GPU OOM messages, scheduler traces.

Status page & customer comms templates

Use these templates on the Status Page (internal canonical copy) and for customer emails/CS messages. Personalize the placeholders (<...>).

Initial acknowledgement (public status page and customer CS)
"We are aware of an issue affecting the Redwood inference API in <region>. Our engineering team is investigating. Impact: increased latency and request failures for some customers. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. Reference: <incident-id>."

Status update (20-60 minute cadence while active)
"Update: Engineering identified a high-error-rate condition tied to <root_cause_short>. We’ve applied a containment step to reduce customer impact by <percent_reduction>% and are validating service behavior. Next update in 30 minutes or after major progress. Impacted customers: <list or 'subset of customers'>. Reference: <incident-id>."

Resolution (final)
"Resolved: The issue affecting inference requests in <region> has been resolved at <time>. Root cause: <short_rca>. Mitigation: <actions taken>. If you continue to experience problems, please contact support with reference <incident-id>. A technical postmortem will be published to customers within 48 hours if they were materially affected."

Internal incident comms cadence (recommended)
- 0-10m: Acknowledgement to core Slack incident channel and create bridge.
- 10-30m: First status update with containment steps completed.
- Every 30m while active: update with metrics and current next-action.
- On resolution: brief summary and link to postmortem draft.

On-call rotation, escalation matrix and shadowing

- Primary responder: 8-hour rotation (08:00–16:00; 16:00–00:00; 00:00–08:00). Relievers shadow for first 48h of a long-running incident.
- Escalation contact order: Primary Pager -> On-call team lead -> SRE Principal -> Head of Infra. Contact details are maintained in the oncall roster.
- Shadowing policy: New responders shadow for 2 full shifts and run tabletop drills before independent paging.

Game days and readiness drills

- Frequency: Quarterly game days per region; monthly tabletop for new hires.
- Exercise types: network partition simulation, multi-model quality regression, capacity exhaustion, and downstream dependency failure.
- Scoring: time-to-detect, time-to-contain, customer-impact reduction, and completeness of evidence collected.

Postmortem and action tracking (must-haves)

1. Postmortem timeline with timestamps for detection, triage, containment, full recovery, and communications.
2. Root cause analysis: a clear causal chain (not just symptoms).
3. Corrective actions: owner, ETA, and verification steps.
4. Customer impact summary and whether credits/notifications are required.
5. Postmortem review meeting scheduled within 7 days and linked in the document.

Evidence collection template (minimum)

- Alert IDs and monitoring graphs (PNG links).
- 3 representative request traces with full call-stack and headers redacted.
- Configuration snapshot (model version, routing rules, autoscale parameters).
- Deployment history for last 24 hours.

When to convert to a public postmortem

- Convert when > 10% of customers or any enterprise customer experienced latency or failures for more than 1 hour, or if the incident required a region-level failover. Publish a customer-facing summary within 48 hours and a full internal RCA within 7 days.

Operational notes & dos-and-don’ts

- Do: Keep the Incident Lead role single-threaded for coordination.
- Do: Avoid broad-spectrum rollbacks without canary validation.
- Do: Use structured ‘degraded-mode’ flags in responses to allow downstream graceful degradation.
- Don’t: Make unilateral security or data-retention changes during an incident.
- Don’t: Use the status page for internal technical noise; keep it high level and customer-centric.

Appendix: CLI snippets and common commands

- Create bridge: redwood bridge create --incident <incident-id> --severity <sev> --owner <il-name>
- Toggle model fallback: redwood routes update --route <route> --fallback-version <id>
- Snapshot deployment: redwood deployments snapshot --service <svc> --out /tmp/snapshot-<ts>.json

Related pages and references

- SLO and error budgeting guidance: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets-2024
- Incident lifecycle templates: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-lifecycle-orchestration-templates-2025
- Runbook maintenance policy: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-retention-and-responder-onboarding-handbook-2026

Document maintenance

- Owner: Engineering (oncall-playbooks squad). Review cadence: quarterly or after any Sev-1 incident.
- Last reviewed: 2025-02-03.

End of document."
